The merge is committed as 5886a6a (condensed into 8251007), and the full test suite passes: 3362 passed, 36 skipped, 37 xfailed, 1 xpassed. Nothing was pushed.

Checks run:

  • Build: just build-ext succeeded.
  • Lint: ruff format and ruff check on tests/ are clean.
  • Targeted files: 310 passed, 7 xfailed, 1 xpassed.
  • Full suite: the result above includes the marker guard in test_suite_contract, which passed. The skips are mostly because matplotlib isn't installed. The one xpass is PB3's own non-strict expected failure for the JAX lossless slab test.

How each conflict was resolved:

  • tests/test_api.py and tests/test_invariants.py: these conflicts came from the RB1 lane, not PA3. I took PB3's side. Its translation-derivative test covers every case RB1 had folded in, at the same tolerances.
  • tests/test_support.py: PB3's structure is kept. PA3's two checks (every exported name is in the catalog, and the slab signature) moved into test_framework_namespaces_share_one_vocabulary.
  • tests/test_torch.py: PB3's side, which moves the duplicated torch gradient tests into the new bridge table in tests/test_adapter_bridges.py. PA3's read-only/negative-stride constant test and its dtype check survived.
  • tests/test_framework_physics.py: rebuilt from PB3's version, with all seven PA3 tests ported to the new engine fixture. Their assertions and tolerances are unchanged. The unknown-polarization check was added to test_framework_physical_mismatches_raise.
    • Two PA3 gradient checks became scenarios (interleaved_slab_thickness, port_wave_second_system), which is how PB3 converted all the others. Advect is checked against finite differences with the same step and tolerances, and JAX and PyTorch must match Advect to 1e-12.

One tolerance changed. The torch vector-wave tuple test depended on a helper PB3 deleted, so it is now a case in test_adapter_bridges.py for both JAX and PyTorch. It now compares against the native pullback to 1e-13 instead of the old finite-difference check at 8e-6, which is stricter. The native pullback is still finite-difference-checked in test_vectorwaves.py, and the standalone JAX version of the test is kept.

PB3's commit message says a deleted torch solve scale test moved to test_linalg.test_linear_solve_common_scale_invariant, but that test doesn't exist; an earlier PB2 commit had already removed it. The property is still covered by a Rust property test and the bridge table's solve cases, and it wasn't a PA3 test, so I kept the deletion. Only the commit message is wrong.
